external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed sensor node installed at a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway
external_entities.notes: The nodes are outside the organisation's physical control. They authenticate to the broker with a fleet-wide pre-shared key.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state what authentication the console has, if any.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views telemetry dashboards from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that accepts readings from sensor nodes and forwards them to Pub/Sub.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE
processes.notes: The gateway is exposed to the internet because nodes dial in from anywhere.

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer in the analytics network that consumes readings and writes them to the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

processes.name: dashboard
processes.description: A dashboard used by fleet operators to view telemetry over BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used by the gateway to check device keys and identify the customer associated with a node.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A Pub/Sub service carrying readings from the device gateway to the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery data store containing sensor telemetry, site addresses, and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket from which sensor nodes poll firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. The source does not state whether nodes verify an image signature before installing it.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: A sensor node publishes readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway.

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up a device in the device registry to check its key and identify its customer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery.

data_flows.name: poll image
data_flows.description: A sensor node polls the firmware bucket for a new firmware image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image and install what they find.
data_flows.notes: The bucket is public read, so node authentication to the bucket is not used.

data_flows.name: service node
data_flows.description: A field technician services a sensor node over its local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what authentication the console has, if any.

data_flows.name: view dashboard
data_flows.description: A fleet operator views dashboards using company SSO.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

data_flows.name: read telemetry
data_flows.description: The dashboard reads telemetry from BigQuery.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery

assumptions.basis: The source states that the registry is used to check the key and find which customer the node belongs to.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is confidential because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns identified as customer data.
assumptions.basis: The source states: "The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data."

assumptions.assumption: The firmware bucket's classification is public because the source explicitly says it is public read.
assumptions.basis: The source states: "The bucket is public read."

assumptions.assumption: The customer-sites boundary is a tenant boundary because the sites are customer-controlled and outside the organisation's physical control.
assumptions.basis: The source states that sensor nodes are installed on customer sites and are outside our physical control.

assumptions.assumption: The GKE boundary is a network boundary because the device gateway is placed in GKE, which is described as its hosting environment.
assumptions.basis: The source states: "an MQTT broker we run on GKE."

assumptions.assumption: The analytics-network boundary is a network boundary because the telemetry normalizer is explicitly placed in the analytics network.
assumptions.basis: The source states: "the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network."

assumptions.assumption: The corporate-network boundary is a network boundary because fleet operators are explicitly placed in the corporate network.
